title: Copyrights taken by smarter men on the Street
summary: Musicians who never knew about copyright lost their tunes to opportunists like arranger Walter Fuller.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: It was a great deal in those days, with you guys just --
-- so happy to be playing with each-other.
Who knew anything about copyrighting material, I mean these guys came along the street and copyrighted all of that, practically all of that stuff. And you turn around and it's gone.

That was one pretty smart guy named Walter Fuller. Not the trumpet player but the arranger. He came walking through the street there and he was calling us fools to our face. He says, you don't do nothing but smoke and drink, you don't know what's going on, and he was stealing all of this stuff, setting himself up in business and every-
And so any way it was so much of that going on it wasn't even funny.
